The proof follows this argument:
- DEF F(t) := (1+t)·log(1+t) − t, so F' = log(1+t) and F(1) = 2·log 2 − 1.
- By the mean value theorem, F(b) − F(a) lies between (b−a)·log(1+a) and (b−a)·log(1+b).
- Summing over the points x^m gives F(1) ≤ (1−x)·T_N ≤ F(1) + (1−x), where T_N = Σ_{m<N} x^m·log(1+x^m). So (1−x)·T_N has a limit Q(x) by monotone convergence.
- The partial log-products satisfy x·L_N = (1−x)·T_N + x^N·log(1+x^N) − log 2, so xprod(x) = exp((Q(x) − log 2)/x).
- Since Q(x) → F(1) as x → 1⁻, xprod(x) → exp(log 2 − 1) = 2/e.
